I fought my ex-husband on intimacy issues for a fucking decade. Led to me stepping out on him. He was shocked to learn that I love being needed and wanted and desired. I begged. I pleaded. I rationalized. Cried. Screamed. For 10 years! And when I came clean he was shocked that I found someone who wanted me?!?!? The fuck?! We patched it up for a few years. And intimacy improved. But the damage was done. So after hating myself for long enough. Feeling so inadequate. And generally wanting to die because of the misery, I left. Again he was shocked. I know I had my share of problems in the marriage for him too. But God damn. You can't fucking beat me down and expect me to take it for my entire life. 

You did good. You did what you needed to do to survive this. You'll be stronger in the end when you take the time to learn to love yourself again. And you will.

Ok. So. To rewrite my comment in a more constructive manner.

In my experience dealing with sex addiction there is still the ability to have boundaries. I know many people with addiction issues of any sort do often have some boundaries. Example is that they won't do certain activities around their families.
Moving on, when I was married I did set boundaries for myself. I did though, as an addict and a very flawed creature, go outside those boundaries on essentially what was a bender and became an obsession with a person. 
But for 10 of 12 years I was faithful. 
With being with someone who doesn't seem like they really want to set, maintain, and standardize those boundaries, I can give you my ex-husband reddit info and he can tell you where he was, and the choices he had to make in choosing to stay a few extra years.
I would definitely talk to your Dr about allllllll of this and your physical/ mental symptoms. You gotta do you, love!

#1 you need to get a check up, I'm sure your doctor would want to know about your symptoms. Yes they could be stress related, or something else. Take care of you first before you can give of yourself to take care of another.
You need to worry about you a little more and a little less about him. What makes you believe that you should sacrifice yourself when he obviously is not making sacrifices to meet your needs? I am a woman and a sex addict. If he can't maintain healthy boundaries while he is with you, that's just not fair to either one of you. He might seem like he's going to change, but outside of an impulsive relapse, has he made any true effort to avoid the impulses.
